correctness.rationale: The repaired RESULT.md retains the correct theorem, rate, and witness. The signed entry map is A−1−Az for A=e^(−κT); independent factors contract from the past since E A<1. Coupling the two entry laws with common ordinary durations bounds their mean difference by 2p_L/[(1−p_L)(1−E_G A)]. The renewal-reward normalization is by the actual mean of each clock. In the equilibrium integrals the ordinary-run entry error then cancels the factor 1−E_G A; it and the exceptional-run exponential relaxation each contribute at most 2Vp_L/(κμ). The two changes of weights each cost at most Vp_Lν/μ by the identity (1−p_L)ν+p_LL=μ. This proves the full Wasserstein estimate. The original limitation incorrectly called the entire limit singular. The corrected text distinguishes its continuous and atomic components, proving absolute continuity of the finite-duration laws by monotone change of variable in age and using the endpoint event to rule out total variation convergence. Both signs have positive-length intervals in the stationary past, ensuring strict interior entry and position. For the witness, the deterministic orbit density and the mixture weights give the stated cumulant. An independent rational enclosure yields K_4>0.0329398020; 16 times the Wasserstein bound at L=300 is 464/14955<0.0329, and the bound decreases thereafter. The mean-one exponential comparator gives moments 1/3 and 1/5, hence −2/15. Replay paths are the frozen verify.py (inspected, not run) and the independently written branches/c24d24d5-a32d-4166-8093-05397f1418f4/independent_witness.py (rational witness calculation, not a proof of the general theorem).

value.rationale: The corrected claim quantifies a natural discontinuity: a perturbation vanishing at renewal epochs keeps a positive fraction of equilibrium time and creates exact endpoint masses, even when the base run law has arbitrary finite-mean tails. The uniform error estimate makes the limiting mechanism observable at a finite duration and turns a qualitative contrast into a provable reversal of the fourth cumulant against a matched-mean clock. The singular-component correction retains this value without overstating the limit.
